# Settings portability: review round 1

Reviewer: Opus 5.5, review only. Diff `git diff c36faf1 3f5eb31 -- app settings.gradle.kts gradle settings_portability settings_android settings_rescue`. Nothing was built or run. No edits outside this file. Over the 30-minute flag (about 45 minutes).

Read in full: ImportCoordinator, ImportJournal, SettingsStores, SettingsCatalog, ConfigurationChecks, LegacyXml, LegacySettingsConverter, codec header and writer; app ProcessStores, SettingsStartup, RecoveryComponents, RecoveryActivity, AndroidSettingsStores, PrivateSettingsFiles, SettingsBackupActivity, the AppModule, MainActivity, manifest and widget diffs; settings_android validator and widget profiles; rescue AdbCommand, RemoteFiles, RemoteShell, AdbShell, CaptureEngine, RescueAdbManager, AdbBridgeService, BridgeSupervision, PrivateFiles, CopiedStores, RescueConverter, RescueConversion, RescueActivity, manifest, build file, strings. Catalog checked against every preference key constant in c36faf1: no missing setting found.

What holds up: journal-first apply, rollback across all three stores, RecoveryRequired never reported as success, reset keys refused on input and removed in the same SharedPreferences commit, raw previous values kept, the strict XML reader, sentinel-based absent-versus-failed listings, stat-before/stat-after plus digest checks, the generation/operation/kind event filter, the binder-liveness kill guard, and the SAF read-back in the helper. A SharedPreferences commit that fails after updating memory still converges, because rollback rewrites the whole file from the restored map.

SCORE[durability]: 6/10 (S1 bricks a healthy app after an update while blocked; S2 leaves the blocked-startup protocol with no executed test; S3 may keep the top-priority rescue from ever completing. Fixing all three raises it to 8-9; bar 9)
SCORE[error-paths]: 6/10 (S3's SOURCE_CHANGED advice cannot be followed; recovery text is wrong after a self-healed launch (nit). Text fixes raise it to 8; bar 6)
SCORE[security]: 8/10 (no in-model exposure: secrets never reach portable files, the journal stays in no_backup, the helper allowlist builds every shell argument from typed input; remaining items are hardening; bar 6)
SCORE[architecture]: 6/10 (S4: the full Gradle build most likely fails while configuring :settings_portability; the shared catalog, converter and validator are the right shape; bar 6)
SCORE[legibility]: 7/10 (claims are cited and sourced; the intro's "Farhan is not changed" is false (S3); bar 6)
VERDICT: CHANGES

S1 [should] [needed for bar: yes] [class: migration-safety] [concern: durability] app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/RecoveryComponents.kt:50, app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/SettingsStartup.kt:16, app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/SettingsStartup.kt:24 `heal()` replays every snapshot entry. If a recorded component no longer exists, the replay calls `setComponentEnabledSetting`, which throws `IllegalArgumentException("Component class … does not exist")`. `SettingsStartup` catches the throw and calls `block()`, so a start with consistent stores (NoImport, Applied or RolledBack) disables everything and skips Hilt. Every later start, and every Retry, throws at the same entry. Reproduction: an import blocks (rollback failed, for example storage full), so the snapshot records all components, including WorkManager's explicit ENABLED proxies. The owner installs a fixed build (the normal pilot loop) that removes or renames one receiver or service, or bumps WorkManager. Every launch now heals, throws, blocks and shows "The recovery state could not be restored". Only clear data, which deletes every setting, or a debuggable `run-as rm` gets out. Fix: in `heal()`, list the current components (the same `getPackageInfo(... GET_DISABLED_COMPONENTS)` that `block()` uses) and skip snapshot entries that are no longer there. A removed component has no state to restore. Pin it with a test from S2.

S2 [should] [needed for bar: yes] [class: test-weakness] [concern: durability] app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/RecoveryComponents.kt:17, app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/ProcessStores.kt:38, app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/SettingsStartup.kt:9 The accepted spec (spec-reply "Tests for green") requires pure JVM tests for the ProcessStores gate (after a blocking result each getter throws and no store opens; no journal opens no store) and for the component protocol over a fake PackageManager: snapshot before the first disable, kill only on change, an upgrade adding a component, exact raw-state healing, a crash after each write, and zero writes on a healthy start. None exist, and the android green report says so. The production journal (`AndroidImportJournal`, which round-trips `previous` through the codec) is covered only by an instrumented test that has not run. The 45 core tests use an in-memory journal. Reproduction by mutation: move `snapshot.write(states)` after the disable loop, call `allowNormalOperation()` before `heal()`, or drop `snapshot.clear()`. All 101 executed tests stay green. S1 is exactly the kind of bug a fake-PackageManager test catches. Fix: put the logic behind a three-method `ComponentStates` port (list, get, set) and a snapshot port, move `block`/`heal` into code the JVM can run, and add the spec's cases plus S1's. Add one ProcessStores gate test with counting store factories. Run the instrumented journal test before round 2.

S3 [should] [needed for bar: yes] [class: misleading-docs] [concern: durability] settings_rescue/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan_rescue/capture/CaptureEngine.kt:109, settings_rescue/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:4, settings_rescue/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:28, settings_rescue/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:93 The capture assumes `am force-stop` keeps the source quiet. On a phone where old Farhan holds notification access (its main feature), NotificationManagerService handles `ACTION_PACKAGE_RESTARTED` through `ManagedServices.onPackagesChanged`, which calls `rebindServices`. Binding the listener also clears the stopped state, so the old Farhan process comes back within seconds. Each arriving notification then writes `farhan_db-wal` and `shared_pref.xml`, the after-stat differs, and the export fails with SOURCE_CHANGED. Its advice, "Make sure it is closed, then try again", cannot be followed. Force-stop also has a second effect. On Android 11-13, `AccessibilityManagerService.onHandleForceStop` removes the package's services from `ENABLED_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICES`, which turns off Farhan's scroll-blocker and grayscale services. The intro's "Farhan is not changed" is therefore false. The stat check fails closed, so no wrong backup is produced. The risk is that the priority-one backup never completes. Reproduction: the owner taps Stop Farhan and export while messages arrive. Copying a multi-megabyte `farhan_db` over loopback spans seconds, so SOURCE_CHANGED keeps repeating. Device check: after force-stop, watch `pidof` for the source and listener rebinding. Smallest fix, with no new commands: `export_body` and `failure_source_changed` tell the owner to turn off Notification access for the old Farhan before exporting and then retry. The intro says force-stop turns off Farhan's accessibility services. The after-save owner steps add turning both back on, or not doing so if the old app is being uninstalled.

S4 [should] [needed for bar: yes] [class: prod-wiring] [concern: architecture] settings_portability/build.gradle.kts:7, build.gradle.kts:9 The module applies `alias(libs.plugins.jetbrainsKotlinJvm)`, which carries version `kotlin`. The root build already puts the Kotlin Gradle plugin artifact on the classpath through `alias(libs.plugins.jetbrainsKotlinAndroid) apply false`. Gradle then refuses the versioned request: "the plugin is already on the classpath with an unknown version, so compatibility cannot be checked". The parent's 101-test run used the standalone `settings_portability/settings.gradle.kts`, which hides this. Reproduction: `nix develop -c make build` fails while configuring `:settings_portability`, before any Android code compiles. Confidence: high, but not run. `./gradlew help` confirms it in seconds. Fix: add `alias(libs.plugins.jetbrainsKotlinJvm) apply false` to the root `plugins {}` block. No module edit is needed.

Accepted design limits (not defects): a Staged journal whose Applying write fails blocks until Retry (conservative, agreed in the spec exchange); the farhan_db-only read; SIZE_ONLY integrity when `sha256sum` is missing; the mass disable's HOME, grant and WorkManager costs (device checks 1-3); the startup join's ANR margin (device check 5). Not checked: libadb, Conscrypt and adbd pairing behaviour; Android compilation beyond S4.

COMMENT-FIXUPS: none

NIT-STASH:
- app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/RecoveryActivity.kt:18 Rollback fails once, the owner opens the recovery icon, and that launch's startup now rolls back and heals. The process continues as a normal one, but the screen still says "Settings recovery is required … could not be restored" because `startupResult` is RolledBack. Show a "recovered, close and reopen" text when `startupResult?.allowsNormalOperation == true`.
- settings_rescue/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan_rescue/adb/AdbShell.kt:47 `lines()` never delivers a final line that lacks a newline. This only affects the informational version dump.
- app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/SettingsBackupActivity.kt:37 The normal app's SAF export does not read the document back, while the helper does (RescueActivity.kt `copyPendingTo`). Reuse the same read-back before "Settings backup saved."
- app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/SettingsBackupActivity.kt:85 The prepared export stays in no_backup if the owner leaves while the unknown-keys dialog is open. It contains configuration only (no secrets), and the next export overwrites it.
- app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/SettingsBackupActivity.kt:97 Failures show raw enum names (`Export refused: TYPE_MISMATCH`). This is fine for the pilot owner. Map them to text before a wider release.

HARDENING-STASH:
- app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/FarhanApplication.kt:31 ACRA 5.12's sender services run in the `:acra` process, so `SettingsStartup` also runs there after a crash. If a crash lands while a journal is Staged, Applying or RollingBack, two processes can apply and roll back concurrently, and one can write Applied over the other's partial rollback. This needs a crash inside a narrow window. Fix: return early in the ACRA sender process (`ACRA.isACRASenderServiceProcess()`), or take a `FileChannel` lock on no_backup around `startup()`/`stage()`.
- app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/PrivateSettingsFiles.kt:84 A previous value the codec cannot encode (a NaN float or a lone surrogate in a string) makes every Applying write fail. The Staged journal then blocks on every start, and the recovery screen has no "discard staged import" action. No current key holds such a value.
- app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/RecoveryComponents.kt:49 A corrupt component snapshot makes `heal()` throw on every start, which leads to `block()` and a permanent block even with consistent stores. AtomicFile makes this unlikely. Treating an unreadable snapshot as "heal what the manifest says" would remove it.
- settings_rescue/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan_rescue/adb/AdbCommand.kt:59 `stat` times have one-second resolution. In SIZE_ONLY mode, a same-second WAL restart between copying `farhan_db` and copying `farhan_db-wal` would go unnoticed. With `sha256sum` present, the digest compare covers changes made during a copy. Changes between copies of different files are still only covered by stat.
- app/src/main/java/ly/com/tahaben/farhan/settings/SettingsBackupActivity.kt:146 `killProcess` right after staging drops pending `SharedPreferences.apply()` writes of keys outside the import domain (ledger, known packages). An explicit `commit()` of an empty edit first would flush them.

Add one JVM test only if the check ends up behind the startup coordinator port. A source-grep test is not worth adding.

No change this round. Nothing has been fixed yet, and S3 and S4 are downgraded in wording, not withdrawn. Security stays at 8.
